entries.title: Main session
entries.summary: One agent owns the task and acceptance.
useWhen: The task is small or tightly coupled.
One decisive source or test can resolve it.
avoidWhen: Independent evidence needs isolation beyond a useful single context.
contract: State the deliverable and verify it.
No delegation call is needed.
entries.example: Fix one documentation typo and check the surrounding instructions.
entries.diagram:
flowchart LR
  T[Task] --> M[Main agent]
  M --> V[Acceptance]
  V --> R[Result]

entries.title: A few ordinary subagents
entries.summary: The main conversation coordinates a few independent assignments.
useWhen: A few small tasks have separate evidence or ownership.
Saving a script provides no useful reuse.
avoidWhen: Many intermediate results overwhelm conversational coordination.
Assignments depend on shared mutable state.
contract: Give each worker a self-contained brief and acceptance.
The main agent reconciles all assignments and integrates.
entries.example: Check two unrelated configuration files against their official documentation.
entries.diagram:
flowchart TD
  M[Main agent] --> A[Config reader A]
  M --> B[Config reader B]
  A --> I[Main integration]
  B --> I
  I --> V[Acceptance]

entries.title: Pipeline
entries.summary: Fixed dependent stages run in order.
useWhen: Later work needs an earlier result.
Stage boundaries provide useful gates or reuse.
avoidWhen: One agent already holds the whole task and scripting adds no value.
contract: Pass checked earlier outputs explicitly.
Stop dependent stages when a required gate fails.
Use adversarial verification when a gate must be independently checked; otherwise outputs remain claims.
entries.example: Inspect a migration, propose a change, then review the proposal in separate dependent stages.
entries.diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[Inspect] --> G[Gate]
  G --> B[Propose]
  B --> H[Gate]
  H --> C[Review]

entries.title: Fleet
entries.summary: A known inventory is partitioned into independent units.
useWhen: Units and ownership are known before launch.
Independent work exceeds its aggregation overhead.
avoidWhen: Workers edit the same shared files.
Integration dominates useful work.
contract: Define stable IDs and aggregation before fan-out.
Bound concurrency and logical calls.
Preserve missing results and reconcile every ID.
Isolate parallel edits in worktrees and verify globally after integration.
entries.example: Audit three independent route groups, then reconcile every route and reproduce findings.
entries.diagram:
flowchart TD
  K[Known inventory] --> A[Unit A]
  K --> B[Unit B]
  K --> C[Unit C]
  A --> R[Reconcile all IDs]
  B --> R
  C --> R
  R --> V[Global acceptance]

entries.title: Independent proposals
entries.summary: Separate agents explore genuinely different approaches to one decision.
useWhen: An ambiguous plan benefits from independent alternatives.
No single decisive source settles the choice.
avoidWhen: Drafts merely repeat one approach.
A simple test resolves the uncertainty.
contract: Fix shared requirements before drafting.
Do not supply sibling outputs to drafters.
Choose select, fuse or a narrow compact-answer vote as the terminal.
entries.example: Compare two API designs against requirements fixed before drafting.
entries.diagram:
flowchart TD
  Q[Common requirements] --> A[Approach A]
  Q --> B[Approach B]
  A --> J[Select / fuse / vote]
  B --> J
  J --> V[Fresh acceptance]

entries.title: Dynamic orchestrator-workers
entries.summary: Discover genuinely unknown subtasks before bounded delegation.
useWhen: A read-only investigation must identify the inventory.
The inventory cannot usefully be specified beforehand.
avoidWhen: Items are already known.
Open-ended branching lacks a scope or ceiling.
contract: Discover the complete in-scope inventory with stable IDs.
If inventory exceeds the selected ceiling, retain it and launch no workers.
Reconcile every discovered item and integrate in the main session.
entries.example: Discover undocumented adapters within one module, then audit each adapter within the selected limit.
entries.diagram:
flowchart TD
  D[Bounded discovery] --> G{Within limit?}
  G -->|No| S[Stop and retain inventory]
  G -->|Yes| W[Independent workers]
  W --> R[Reconcile]
  R --> V[Acceptance]

entries.title: Adversarial verification
entries.summary: A separate invocation tries to falsify a candidate.
useWhen: Claims need reproduction, counterexamples or source checks.
A quality gate warrants an independent check.
avoidWhen: The reviewer cannot access the relevant artifacts or evidence.
A rhetorical disagreement is treated as validation.
contract: Verify actual artifacts against acceptance.
Report passed, failed or inconclusive with evidence.
Same-model invocations can share failure modes.
entries.example: Try to reproduce each reported authentication bypass before accepting it.
entries.diagram:
flowchart LR
  W[Candidate] --> V[Independent verifier]
  V --> P[Passed]
  V --> F[Failed / inconclusive]

entries.title: Bounded iteration
entries.summary: Repair against external feedback within explicit limits.
useWhen: An external rubric or check can identify improvement.
Focused repairs can address stable failing checks.
avoidWhen: No useful acceptance or progress indicator exists.
Self-approval replaces external evidence.
contract: Requires adversarial verification in the bundled executor.
Set maximum rounds and calls before launch.
Stop on acceptance, repeated failing check IDs or the ceiling.
entries.example: Repair a unit for at most two rounds and stop if the same external failure repeats.
entries.diagram:
flowchart LR
  W[Work] --> E[External evaluation]
  E -->|Pass| D[Done]
  E -->|Fail within limit| R[Focused repair]
  R --> E
  E -->|Repeated / limit| S[Stop]

entries.title: Select one proposal
useWhen: One approach should own the final artifact.
A fixed rubric distinguishes viable options.
avoidWhen: No candidate meets the acceptance criteria.
A new combined artifact is actually needed.
contract: Fix the rubric before drafting.
Assess every candidate and criterion with evidence.
Select exactly one existing ID; all its rubric verdicts must pass.
Judge claims still require actual acceptance checks.
entries.example: Choose one API proposal that satisfies every fixed acceptance criterion.
entries.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[Proposal A] --> J[Fixed rubric]
  B[Proposal B] --> J
  J --> S[One intact proposal]
  S --> V[Acceptance]

entries.title: Fuse complementary proposals
entries.summary: Create a new synthesis from compatible, attributed elements.
useWhen: Different approaches contain useful complementary elements.
Contradictions can be resolved explicitly.
avoidWhen: Combining incompatible assumptions hides a decision.
Concatenation is mistaken for synthesis.
contract: Fix the rubric before drafting and retain complete scorecards.
Track provenance and explain rejected elements.
Resolve unknowns and contradictions in main-session acceptance.
A fusion is a new artifact; prior candidate checks do not validate it.
entries.example: Combine a simple public API with another proposal's failure-handling strategy, then test the combined design.
entries.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[Proposal A] --> F[Attributed synthesis]
  B[Proposal B] --> F
  F --> C[Resolve contradictions]
  C --> V[Fresh acceptance]

entries.title: Vote on a compact answer
entries.summary: Count exact compact answers using a strict majority.
useWhen: The output is one exact, narrow answer.
Each candidate has independent supporting evidence.
avoidWhen: The output is code, architecture or a preference.
Agreement is treated as truth.
contract: Use compactAnswer=true; no proposal rubric.
Require a nonempty single-line answer of at most 256 characters.
A strict majority is required; ties stay unresolved.
Verify the winning answer separately.
entries.example: Compare independently derived exact identifiers, then verify the majority identifier against the primary source.
entries.diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[Exact answers] --> M{Strict majority?}
  M -->|Yes| V[Verify answer]
  M -->|No| U[Unresolved]
